description: "The case snapshot, evidence records, authority decisions and explicit decisions canon evaluate reads, the decision it writes, and the properties canon check reads."

Generated from the model types in [`crates/canon/src/model`](https://github.com/beyond10x/canon/blob/main/crates/canon/src/model). `canon evaluate` reads a compiled protocol, one case snapshot, a set of evidence records and, optionally, a list of authority decisions and a list of explicit decisions, and writes a decision. `canon check` reads a protocol and, optionally, the properties declared beside it. Every key is listed; a key Canon does not know is refused.

## `canon-case/1`

Read by `canon evaluate`. The [JSON Schema](https://beyond10x.github.io/canon/schemas/case-1.schema.json) is generated from the same types.

### `Case`

A `canon-case/1` case snapshot as written.

| Key | Value | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | text | required | The document format; the evaluator accepts only `canon-case/1`. |
| `id` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`CaseId`) | required | — |
| `protocol` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`ProtocolId`) | required | The protocol that governs the case. |
| `artifacts` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`ArtifactId`) to [`CaseArtifact`](#caseartifact) | required | The current revision of each declared artifact, keyed by artifact id. |
| `termination` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`OutcomeId`) | optional | The outcome the case terminated through; absent while the case is open. Whether the protocol declares it is checked by the outcomes section (story:outcomes). |
| `revision` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`Revision`) | optional | The case's own current revision. An explicit decision applies only while its `case_revision` is this one; a snapshot without one has no explicit decision applying. |
| `inputs` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`InputId`) to [identifier](#identifiers) (`InputValue`) | optional | The value of each case input, keyed by input id, fixed when the case opens. Left out by a case of a protocol that declares no input. |
| `independence` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`Principal`) to list of [identifier](#identifiers) (`IndependenceDimensionId`) | optional | The dimensions on which each producer is independent of the case's work, keyed by producer, as the trusted context that writes the case resolved them. A producer absent from it, or listed with `[]`, is independent on no dimension. |

### `CaseArtifact`

One declared artifact as the case snapshot records it.

| Key | Value | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `revision` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`Revision`) | required | The artifact's current revision. |

## `canon-evidence/1`

Read by `canon evaluate`. The [JSON Schema](https://beyond10x.github.io/canon/schemas/evidence-1.schema.json) is generated from the same types.

### `EvidenceRecord`

One `canon-evidence/1` record as written. `subject` and `subject_revision` bind it: the
evaluator refuses a record whose subject the protocol does not declare, and applies a record
only while its subject revision is the case's current revision of that subject.

| Key | Value | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | text | required | The document format; the evaluator accepts only `canon-evidence/1`. |
| `id` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`EvidenceId`) | required | — |
| `kind` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`EvidenceKindId`) | required | The evidence kind, which the protocol declares. |
| `result` | text | optional | What the observation found; a record without one matches only an evidence match that names no result. |
| `subject` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`ArtifactId`) | required | The artifact the record is about. |
| `subject_revision` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`Revision`) | required | The revision of that artifact the record is about. |
| `observed_at` | [text](#text-formats) (`Instant`) | optional | When the observation was made; its age at the evaluation instant is measured from here. A record without it never expires. |
| `upstream_revisions` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`ArtifactId`) to [identifier](#identifiers) (`Revision`) | optional | The revision of each upstream artifact the observation was made against, keyed by artifact. A record without it is never invalidated. |
| `producer` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`Principal`) | optional | Who produced the record, recorded as given: Canon does not prove it. A record without one is of no evidence match that demands independence. |
| `child_case` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`CaseId`) | optional | The child case a `case_outcome` record is about (story:case-composition): one record per child case, its `result` the child's outcome, `open` while the child runs. Written only on a `case_outcome` record, which must name its child and give an outcome. |

## `canon-decision/1`

Written by `canon evaluate`.

### `Decision`

A `canon-decision/1` document. A section slot that is `None` is not serialized.

| Key | Value | Present | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | text | always | Always `canon-decision/1`. |
| `case` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`CaseId`) | always | — |
| `protocol` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`ProtocolId`) | always | — |
| `protocol_revision` | integer, 0 or more | always | The revision of the compiled protocol that applied. |
| `claims` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`ClaimId`) to [`ClaimDecision`](#claimdecision) | always | Every declared claim, in identifier order. |
| `obligations` | any JSON value | when present | Each declared obligation, in identifier order, with its `ObligationStatus`; written when the protocol declares an obligation. Its shape is fixed by CANON-OBLIGATION-001 and, for an obligation with an applicability predicate, CANON-INPUT-001. |
| `actions` | any JSON value | when present | Each declared action, `admissible`, `approval-required` or `blocked`, with the reasons for a status other than `admissible`; written when the protocol declares an action. Its shape is fixed by CANON-AUTHORITY-001. |
| `outcomes` | any JSON value | when present | Each declared outcome, `legitimate` or `blocked`, with the reasons it is blocked; written when the protocol declares an outcome. Its shape is fixed by CANON-OUTCOME-001 and, for an outcome that requires an explicit decision, by CANON-OUTCOME-002: a legitimate one records `decided_by` (`{"decision": <name>, "principals": [...]}`), and a blocked one gives the reason `{"decision": <name>, "present": false}`. |
| `explanation` | any JSON value | when present | Why each claim that is not `true`, each open obligation, each action that is not admissible and each blocked outcome has its status, traced to the evidence records that applied or were excluded, and what the decision was computed from (`computed_from`); the evaluator writes it on every decision. Its shape is fixed by CANON-EXPLAIN-001. |
| `missing_evidence` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`ActionId`) to list of [identifier](#identifiers) (`EvidenceKindId`) | when present | For each admissible action whose `may_produce` is not empty, the evidence kinds of that list that have no applicable record, in kind-identifier order; an empty list means every kind it may produce has one. Written only when some action qualifies. An action that is blocked or approval-required, and one whose `may_produce` is empty, is not listed. A record is applicable when the revision-binding and freshness stages leave it and no claim lists it in its `excluded_evidence`. Its shape is fixed by CANON-FRONTIER-001. |
| `pending_decisions` | any JSON value | when present | The decisions the evaluation waits on, each a `canon-authority/1` or `canon-decisions/1` entry that would change a status in this decision; written only when there is one. Under `authority`, one entry per requirement an `approval-required` action names with the decision `none` or `require_approval`: `{"action", "capability", "scope", "current", "case_revision", "options": ["granted", "denied"]}`, `current` being that decision, `scope` written when the requirement has one and `case_revision`, the case snapshot's revision, when it has one. A blocked action has none. Ordered by action, then capability, then scope: no scope first, then two scopes by their key-value pairs in key order, compared pair by pair, key before value, a scope that is a prefix of the other first. Under `decisions`, one entry per outcome blocked for want of an explicit decision, `{"outcome", "decision", "case_revision", "options": ["taken"]}`, in outcome order; for a snapshot without a revision it has no `case_revision` and the options `[]`, as no explicit decision can apply. Each list is left out when empty. An option is the value of the entry a caller would add, with its own principal; precedence does not change, so a `granted` entry decides a requirement whose `current` is `require_approval` only when no `require_approval` entry still covers it. Its shape is fixed by CANON-PENDING-001. |

### `ClaimDecision`

One claim's entry in a decision.

| Key | Value | Present | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | [`Truth`](./protocol.md#truth) | always | — |
| `excluded_evidence` | list of [`EvidenceExclusion`](#evidenceexclusion) | when not empty | The evidence an exclusion stage kept from this claim, in evidence-id order. Empty unless a stage excluded something; an empty list is not serialized. |

### `EvidenceExclusion`

One evidence record an exclusion stage kept from a claim, and why.

| Key | Value | Present | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evidence` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`EvidenceId`) | always | — |
| `reason` | [`ExclusionReason`](#exclusionreason) | always | — |

### `ExclusionReason`

Why evidence was excluded: before claims were evaluated, or, for `NotIndependent`, from the
evidence matches that demand an independence its producer lacks.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `revision_mismatch` | Bound to a revision of its subject that is not the current one. |
| `expired` | Older than its kind allows at the evaluation instant. |
| `invalidated` | Invalidated by an invalidation rule. |
| `not_independent` | Produced by a producer the case does not list as independent on every dimension an evidence match demands. |

## `canon-authority/1`

Read by `canon evaluate --authority`: a list of `AuthorityDecision` entries; an empty list is allowed. Two entries equal in capability, scope (the same keys with the same values, in any order), case revision and principal are refused, whatever the decision; the JSON Schema cannot express that, and refuses only an entry repeated exactly. The [JSON Schema](https://beyond10x.github.io/canon/schemas/authority-1.schema.json) is generated from the same types.

### `AuthorityDecision`

One entry of a `canon-authority/1` document: a capability, the scope the decision covers, the
decision and, optionally, who took it, the case revision it was taken at and the grounds it
rested on.

| Key | Value | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`CapabilityId`) | required | The capability decided, an identifier an action's `requires` may name. |
| `scope` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`ScopeKey`) to [identifier](#identifiers) (`ScopeValue`) | optional | The scope the decision covers: one value for each key it names, each key once. It covers a requirement of its capability when the requirement gives each of those keys the same value; a key it leaves out covers every value of it. Absent or empty, it covers every scope. |
| `decision` | [`Grant`](#grant) | required | Whether it is granted. |
| `principal` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`Principal`) | optional | Who took it, an identifier, recorded as given: Canon resolves no identity, so it is matched against nothing and does not change admissibility. |
| `case_revision` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`Revision`) | optional | The case revision it was taken at, an identifier: the decision applies only while the case snapshot's `revision` equals it, and to nothing when the snapshot has none. Absent, it applies at every case revision. |
| `ground_revisions` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`ArtifactId`) to [identifier](#identifiers) (`Revision`) | optional | The artifact revisions the decision rested on, keyed by artifact, each key once (story:decision-grounds): a ground holds while its revision is the case snapshot's current revision of the artifact, compared for equality. The decision applies only while every ground holds, whatever it decided. Absent or empty, it rests on no artifact. |
| `ground_evidence` | list of [identifier](#identifiers) (`EvidenceId`) | optional | The evidence records the decision rested on, by id: a ground holds while a record with that id is applicable, the rule of `missing_evidence` (given, left by the revision-binding and freshness stages, and listed in no claim's `excluded_evidence`), so expiry and invalidation reach the decision through it. An id no record has does not hold and is not refused. Absent or empty, it rests on no record. |

### `Grant`

An authority decision on one capability at one scope. Among the decisions covering a
requirement, `denied` wins over `require_approval`, which wins over `granted`; none covering it
is not granted. With its precondition `true`, an action is `admissible` when every requirement
is granted, `blocked` when one is denied, and `approval-required` when none is denied and one
requires approval or is not decided.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `granted` | The capability is granted. |
| `require_approval` | The capability is granted only with approval: asking for approval could grant it. |
| `denied` | The capability is denied; asking again would not change it. |

## `canon-decisions/1`

Read by `canon evaluate --decisions`: a list of `ExplicitDecision` entries; an empty list is allowed. An entry given twice, every key equal, is refused. The [JSON Schema](https://beyond10x.github.io/canon/schemas/decisions-1.schema.json) is generated from the same types.

### `ExplicitDecision`

One entry of a `canon-decisions/1` document. It applies to `outcome` when the outcome requires
a decision named `decision`, `case_revision` is the case snapshot's revision and every ground
holds.

| Key | Value | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decision` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`DecisionName`) | required | Which decision was taken. |
| `outcome` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`OutcomeId`) | required | The outcome it was taken for. |
| `principal` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`Principal`) | required | Who took it. |
| `case_revision` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`Revision`) | required | The case revision it was taken at. |
| `ground_revisions` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`ArtifactId`) to [identifier](#identifiers) (`Revision`) | optional | The artifact revisions the decision rested on, keyed by artifact, each key once (story:decision-grounds): a ground holds while its revision is the case snapshot's current revision of the artifact, compared for equality. Absent or empty, it rests on no artifact. |
| `ground_evidence` | list of [identifier](#identifiers) (`EvidenceId`) | optional | The evidence records the decision rested on, by id: a ground holds while a record with that id is applicable, the rule of `missing_evidence` (given, left by the revision-binding and freshness stages, and listed in no claim's `excluded_evidence`), so expiry and invalidation reach the decision through it. An id no record has does not hold and is not refused. Absent or empty, it rests on no record. |

## `canon-properties/1`

Read by `canon check --properties`. The [JSON Schema](https://beyond10x.github.io/canon/schemas/properties-1.schema.json) is generated from the same types.

### `Properties`

A `canon-properties/1` document as written.

| Key | Value | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | text | required | The document format; `canon check` accepts only `canon-properties/1`. |
| `protocol` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`ProtocolId`) | required | The id of the protocol the properties are about; `canon check` refuses another. |
| `properties` | map from [identifier](#identifiers) (`PropertyId`) to [`Property`](#property) | optional | The properties, keyed by identifier. A property declared twice is refused. |

### `Property`

One property: its subject's status is the same in every two states that agree on everything
except the evidence the `independent_of` claim reads.

| Key | Value | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | optional | — |
| `subject` | [`PropertySubject`](#propertysubject) | required | The action or outcome whose status the property is about. |
| `independent_of` | [`PropertyDependency`](#propertydependency) | required | What the subject's status must not depend on. |

### `PropertySubject`

What a property is about. Written as a map with exactly one of the keys `action` or `outcome`.

| Key | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`ActionId`) | The action's status: `admissible`, `approval-required` or `blocked`. |
| `outcome` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`OutcomeId`) | The outcome's status: `legitimate` or `blocked`. |

### `PropertyDependency`

What a property's subject must not depend on. Written as a map with the one key `claim`.

| Key | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | [identifier](#identifiers) (`ClaimId`) | The claim, standing for the evidence it reads, by kind and subject, directly or through the claims it tests. |

## Identifiers

An identifier is text. A well-formed identifier is not empty, and without whitespace, control characters or Unicode format characters (general category Cf). Each kind of identifier is its own type, so one cannot stand in for another. These are the kinds these documents use:

| Type | Identifies |
|---|---|
| `ScopeKey` | A key of a capability scope (`cluster`, `namespace`): what the scope narrows the capability to. An identifier. |
| `ScopeValue` | The value a capability scope gives one key (`prod-eu`). An identifier. |
| `ProtocolId` | Identifies a protocol, independently of its revision. |
| `CaseId` | Identifies one case governed by a protocol. |
| `ArtifactId` | Identifies an artifact a protocol declares. |
| `Revision` | Identifies one revision of an artifact, or of the case itself: the case snapshot's own revision, and the case revision an explicit decision was taken at. |
| `ClaimId` | Identifies a claim a protocol declares. |
| `EvidenceId` | Identifies one evidence record. |
| `EvidenceKindId` | Identifies a kind of evidence a protocol declares. |
| `ActionId` | Identifies an action a protocol declares. |
| `OutcomeId` | Identifies an outcome a protocol declares. |
| `CapabilityId` | Names a capability an action requires authority for. |
| `DecisionName` | Names an explicit decision an outcome may require (`explicitly_inconclusive`). |
| `Principal` | Who took an explicit decision, or who produced an evidence record, recorded as given: Canon resolves no identity and proves no production. |
| `IndependenceDimensionId` | Identifies an independence dimension a protocol declares (`different_principal`). Canon gives no dimension a meaning; the trusted context that writes the case resolves it. |
| `InputId` | Identifies a case input a protocol declares. |
| `InputValue` | One value a case input may take: an identifier its input declares. Read from any scalar, alike in the protocol and in the case: `values: [true, false]` declares the values `true` and `false`, and a case gives one as `flag: true`. |
| `PropertyId` | Identifies one property of a `canon-properties/1` document. |

## Text formats

These values are text in a fixed form, not identifiers. Canon refuses text that does not match its pattern, and also checks what the pattern cannot:

| Type | Written as | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `Instant` | An instant written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC, or with a fraction of one to nine digits after the seconds, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ`; uppercase `T` and `Z`, no leap second (`2026-10-04T12:00:00Z`, `2026-10-04T12:00:00.400Z`): when evidence was observed, and the evaluation instant. Order forms compare every instant of one evaluation at one resolution, the coarsest precision written among its records, dropping finer digits (`12:00:00.4Z` beside `12:00:00Z` reads as `12:00:00Z`); expiry reads the whole seconds and ignores the fraction. Calendar validity is checked by Canon, not by the pattern: the date must exist (leap years included) and the time be at most 23:59:59. | `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]{1,9})?Z$` |
